Topics · Is there a God?

Isn't morality just something humans made up?

It lives in humans, and everyone has a conscience, believer or not. What does 'that is unjust' appeal to?

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّىٰهَا٧ فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَىٰهَا٨ قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّىٰهَا٩ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَن دَسَّىٰهَا١٠﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [by] the soul and He who proportioned it[1932] And inspired it [with discernment of] its wickedness and its righteousness, He has succeeded who purifies it, And he has failed who instills it [with corruption].

Translator's notes

[1932] i.e., balanced and refined it, creating in it sound tendencies and consciousness.

Quran · Ash-Shams 91:7-10

Translation

(for when Gentiles who don’t have the law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having the law, are a law to themselves, in that they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience testifying with them, and their thoughts among themselves accusing or else excusing them)

Original · Ancient Greek

ὅταν γὰρ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ νόμον ἔχοντα φύσει τὰ τοῦ νόμου ποιῶσιν, οὗτοι νόμον μὴ ἔχοντες ἑαυτοῖς εἰσιν νόμος· οἵτινες ἐνδείκνυνται τὸ ἔργον τοῦ νόμου γραπτὸν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν, συμμαρτυρούσης αὐτῶν τῆς συνειδήσεως καὶ μεταξὺ ἀλλήλων τῶν λογισμῶν κατηγορούντων ἢ καὶ ἀπολογουμένων,

Romans · 2:14-15

World English Bible

In one sense, yes, and this argument does not deny it. Morality lives in human beings. Children protest unfairness before they can spell it. Non-believers are honest and kind. It does not need a religion to install it. This passage agrees: it says that knowing right from wrong is part of being a soul at all. It speaks of every soul, with no condition of faith. So the claim that people need scripture to be good is not what this text says.

A question for you

Where did your strongest sense of right and wrong come from?

If you sayFrom my family and upbringing.
ThenThey played a large part. It leaves the question of how you could criticise anything they taught you.
If you sayFrom how humans evolved.
ThenThat is a good account of how the sense arose. Another question follows.
If you sayFrom my own experience and people's suffering.
ThenThat is a living source, and it shows that morality is not arithmetic for you.

Ecclesiastes · 12:14

World English Bible

A related thing has to be said. Some people have been told, or implied, that those without religion cannot be good. That is false, and this app will never say it. By the text's own measure, no good deed goes unrecognised. Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. Those lines, taken alone, name no membership test. How such goodness is met in the next life belongs to God, who is just and merciful. Whether it is real is not in doubt. A kind atheist is kind.

Original · Hebrew

וְאַתָּ֖ה בֵּאלֹהֶ֣יךָ תָשׁ֑וּב חֶ֤סֶד וּמִשְׁפָּט֙ שְׁמֹ֔ר וְקַוֵּ֥ה אֶל־אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ תָּמִֽיד׃

Hosea · 12:6

World English Bible

Now the question that remains. If morality is only human, what are you saying when you say 'slavery was wrong, even though most people accepted it'? Not that you dislike it. You mean it was wrong then, for them. Then the claim appeals to something beyond what anyone feels. Some accept the cost and call moral claims neither true nor false. Others hold moral truths without God. This argument asks what such truths are and why they would bind us. The verses name an inner witness and commanded justice.

A question for you

When you say 'this is unjust even if everyone accepts it', what do you mean?

If you sayThat I personally reject it.
ThenThen the sentence describes your feeling. It tells the oppressor not that he is wrong, only that you disagree.
If you sayThat it is a moral truth, without God.
ThenThat is a serious position. The question for it is what that truth is, and how we know it.
If you sayThat it goes against what makes people flourish.
ThenThat is a strong standard. It leaves why another's flourishing should bind me when it conflicts with mine.
If you sayI don't know.
ThenMany philosophers do not know either. There is an older question on this.
